title: Asian Art Beyond Ukiyo-e
description: Chinese, Korean, Persian, and Indian masterworks of brush, ink, and gold across a thousand years.
source: Cleveland Museum of Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Finches and bamboo
items.medium: Handscroll; ink and color on silk
items.description_narrative: This exquisite handscroll, 'Finches and bamboo,' showcases delicate ink and color on silk. Created by Emperor Huizong, it captures a serene moment in nature with meticulous detail.
items.tags: nature, birds, bamboo, Chinese art, ink painting, silk, handscroll, imperial

items.title: Old Trees, Level Distance
items.medium: Handscroll; ink and color on silk
items.description_narrative: This intricate handscroll by Guo Xi captures the essence of a vast landscape, rendered in ink and color on silk. Distant mountains and ancient trees emerge from mist, inviting contemplation of nature's grandeur and the artist's skillful brushwork.
items.tags: landscape, nature, handscroll, ink, silk, chinese, song dynasty, traditional

items.title: Travelers Among Mountains and Streams
items.description_narrative: Fan Kuan's monumental ink landscape depicts a towering central peak dominating a scene of deep valleys, waterfalls, and mist-shrouded forests. Tiny figures of travelers and their mules, along with a hidden temple, highlight the vast scale of nature and humanity's small place within it.
items.tags: chinese landscape painting, song dynasty, monumental, ink, nature, mountains, travelers, grandeur

items.title: Early Spring
items.cultural_context: Northern Song Dynasty, Chinese landscape painting
items.description_narrative: This monumental hanging scroll captures the essence of a mountainous landscape emerging from winter, with towering peaks, winding streams, and delicate trees rendered with intricate brushwork. Guo Xi's innovative 'cloud-and-mist' technique imbues the scene with a sense of atmospheric depth and ethereal tranquility.
items.tags: landscape, mountains, chinese painting, song dynasty, shanshui, atmospheric, tranquility

items.title: Night Revels of Han Xizai
items.description_narrative: This iconic handscroll vividly depicts the nocturnal revels of Han Xizai, a high-ranking official during China's Southern Tang dynasty. Commissioned to document the minister's private life, it offers a detailed look at various scenes of entertainment and social interaction.
items.tags: chinese painting, handscroll, court life, figure painting, 10th century, tang dynasty, narrative, banquet

items.title: Summer Mountains
items.description_narrative: This artwork, titled 'Summer Mountains,' presents a landscape scene featuring prominent mountainous formations. Created by the artist Qu Ding, it exemplifies a traditional approach to depicting natural vistas.
items.tags: landscape, mountains, Chinese art, nature, serene, traditional

items.title: The Court of Gayumars
items.description_narrative: This intricate Persian miniature depicts the legendary first king of Persia, Gayumars, enthroned amidst a vibrant, mountainous landscape. Surrounded by his court, animals, and mythical beings, the artwork exemplifies the rich narrative tradition and detailed artistry of Persian manuscript illumination.
items.tags: persian miniature, safavid, manuscript illumination, mythology, court scene, vibrant, detailed, narrative

items.title: Folio from the Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp
items.description_narrative: This folio is a page from the monumental Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp, a lavishly illustrated manuscript of Ferdowsi's epic Persian poem. It exemplifies the peak of Safavid miniature painting, renowned for its intricate detail, vibrant colors, and sophisticated composition.
items.tags: persian, safavid, manuscript, miniature painting, epic poetry, illumination, narrative, rich

items.title: Folio from the Hamzanama
items.description_narrative: This vibrant folio is a page from the Hamzanama, a grand illuminated manuscript commissioned by the Mughal emperor Akbar. It depicts a narrative scene from the adventures of Hamza, showcasing the distinctive artistic style and storytelling tradition of the Mughal court.
items.tags: mughal, hamzanama, manuscript, narrative, indian art, illumination, epic

items.title: Krishna Lifting Mount Govardhan
items.cultural_context: Northern India, Himachal Pradesh, Pahari Kingdom of Kangra
items.medium: gum tempera and gold on paper
items.description_narrative: This vibrant painting depicts the Hindu deity Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan, sheltering his devotees from the wrath of the god Indra. Executed with gum tempera and gold on paper, it exemplifies the refined artistic traditions of the Pahari school in Northern India.
items.tags: krishna, hinduism, pahari, indian painting, kangra school, devotional, myth, tempera

items.title: Pine Trees Screen
items.description_narrative: Hasegawa Tōhaku's "Pine Trees Screen" is a pair of six-panel folding screens, celebrated for its innovative use of ink wash to depict a misty forest. Through atmospheric perspective and subtle gradations of sumi ink, the work evokes a deep sense of stillness and the spiritual essence of nature.
items.tags: landscape, ink wash, suibokuga, momoyama, nature, serene, screens, monochrome

items.title: Wind God and Thunder God
items.cultural_context: Rinpa School, Early Edo period, Japanese
items.description_narrative: This iconic pair of two-fold screens depicts the dynamic deities Fūjin, the Wind God, and Raijin, the Thunder God, caught in dramatic motion. Sōtatsu's bold brushwork and use of gold leaf create a vibrant, swirling energy that captures the power of these elemental forces.
items.tags: japanese art, shinto, deities, wind god, thunder god, rimpa, screen painting, dynamic

items.title: Red and White Plum Blossoms
items.description_narrative: Ogata Kōrin's iconic "Red and White Plum Blossoms" depicts two blossoming plum trees on a shimmering gold ground, separated by a stylized stream. This vibrant pair of two-fold screens showcases the artist's masterful use of bold outlines and color fields, creating a dynamic and decorative landscape.
items.tags: plum blossoms, nature, screens, rinpa school, japanese art, landscape, gold leaf, decorative

items.title: Irises Screen
items.description_narrative: Two six-fold screens vividly depict a field of irises in bloom, rendered with broad strokes of color and gold on paper. This iconic work by Ogata Kōrin is a masterful example of the Rinpa school's decorative and stylized aesthetic.
items.tags: irises, flowers, gold leaf, screen painting, rinpa school, edo period, japanese art, nature

items.title: The Concourse of the Birds
items.medium: Ink, watercolor, and gold on paper
items.description_narrative: Illustrating a scene from Attar's mystical poem "The Conference of the Birds," dozens of birds gather around the wise hoopoe amid a richly patterned Safavid landscape. Its intricate gold detailing and dense symbolism make it one of the most celebrated pages of Persian manuscript painting.
items.tags: safavid, persian miniature, sufi poetry, manuscript illumination, gold leaf, mysticism

items.title: Fish and Rocks
items.description_narrative: A few sparse fish drift beneath looming, abstracted rocks conjured in spare, wet strokes of ink. A Ming imperial descendant who became a Buddhist monk, Bada Shanren charged such minimalist images with veiled melancholy and quiet defiance.

items.title: Cypress Trees
items.medium: Ink, color and gold leaf on paper, folding screen
items.description_narrative: A colossal, gnarled cypress writhes across gilded panels streaked with gold clouds and blue water. Its bold scale and shimmering ground define the grand decorative manner Eitoku devised for the castles of Japan's warlords.

items.title: Youth Holding a Pomegranate
items.medium: Ink and color on paper, single-page miniature
items.description_narrative: An elegant youth in a gold-patterned robe holds a pomegranate, his figure drawn in a single graceful, calligraphic contour. Reza Abbasi, court painter to Shah Abbas I, was the last great master of the Persian miniature.

items.title: Tobatsu Bishamonten
items.medium: Zelkova wood with traces of color
items.description_narrative: This majestic sculpture depicts Tobatsu Bishamonten, a powerful guardian deity, meticulously carved from zelkova wood with subtle traces of original color. Originating from Japan, it represents a significant example of religious artistry from the late 10th to early 11th century.
items.tags: buddhist deity, sculpture, wood carving, japanese art, religious, medieval, guardian
